sources.snippet: 👉 [Microsoft Research Blog Post](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-unlocking-llm-discovery-on-narrative-private-data/). GraphRAG is a structured, hierarchical approach to Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), as opposed to naive semantic-search. The GraphRAG process involves extracting a knowledge graph out of raw text, building a community hierarchy, generating summaries for these communities, and then leveraging these structures when perform RAG-based tasks. To learn more about GraphRAG and how it can be used to enhance your language model's ability to reason about your private data, please visit the [Microsoft Research Blog Post](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-unlocking-llm-discovery-on-narrative-private-data/). ## GraphRAG vs Baseline RAG 🔍. GraphRAG uses knowledge graphs to provide substantial improvements in question-and-answer performance when reasoning about complex information. Microsoft Research’s new approach, GraphRAG, creates a knowledge graph based on an input corpus. This graph, along with community summaries and graph machine learning outputs, are used to augment prompts at query time. GraphRAG builds upon our prior [research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/patterns-hidden-inside-the-org-chart) and [tooling](https://github.com/graspologic-org/graspologic) using graph machine learning. Please see the [breaking changes](https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag/blob/main/breaking-changes.md) document for notes on our approach to versioning the project.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Graphs (GraphRAG) - arXiv
sources.snippet: # Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Graphs (GraphRAG). Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a powerful technique that enhances downstream task execution by retrieving additional information, such as knowledge, skills, and tools from external sources. Graph, by its intrinsic "nodes connected by edges" nature, encodes massive heterogeneous and relational information, making it a golden resource for RAG in tremendous real-world applications. As a result, we have recently witnessed increasing attention on equipping RAG with Graph, i.e., GraphRAG. However, unlike conventional RAG, where the retriever, generator, and external data sources can be uniformly designed in the neural-embedding space, the uniqueness of graph-structured data, such as diverse-formatted and domain-specific relational knowledge, poses unique and significant challenges when designing GraphRAG for different domains. Our survey first proposes a holistic GraphRAG framework by defining its key components, including query processor, retriever, organizer, generator, and data source. The retrieved content is then refined by an organizer and seamlessly integrated with the original query or instruction, which is further fed into the generator to produce the final answer.

sources.title: GraphRAG Explained: Enhancing RAG with Knowledge Graphs
sources.snippet: # GraphRAG Explained: Enhancing RAG with Knowledge Graphs | by Zilliz | Medium. # GraphRAG Explained: Enhancing RAG with Knowledge Graphs. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that connects external data sources to enhance the output of large language models) (LLMs). A baseline RAG usually integrates a vector database and an LLM, where the vector database stores and retrieves contextual information for user queries, and the LLM generates answers based on the retrieved context. For example, consider this question: “_What name was given to the son of the man who defeated the usurper Allectus?”_. To address such challenges, Microsoft Research introduced GraphRAG, a brand-new method that augments RAG retrieval and generation with knowledge graphs. In the following sections, we’ll explain how GraphRAG works under the hood and how to run it with the Milvusvector database. Unlike a baseline RAG that uses a vector database to retrieve semantically similar text, GraphRAG enhances RAG by incorporating knowledge graphs (KGs).

### GraphRAG: A State-of-the-Art Approach to Retrieval Augmented Generation

GraphRAG is an innovative framework designed to enhance the capabilities of language models in Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) tasks through the integration of knowledge graphs. This structured and hierarchical approach addresses the complexities of information retrieval and reasoning, providing a more effective means of generating responses to complex queries compared to traditional RAG systems.

#### Key Components and Process

The GraphRAG process begins with the extraction of a knowledge graph from raw text. This graph represents relational and heterogeneous information, which is crucial for understanding the context of the data. Following this, a community hierarchy is constructed, allowing for the organization of information into manageable segments. Summaries are then generated for these communities, which play a pivotal role during RAG tasks by providing focused insights [1].

GraphRAG's architecture includes several essential components: a query processor, retriever, organizer, generator, and data source. These elements work in concert to refine and integrate the retrieved content with the original query, ensuring that the responses generated are not only relevant but also contextually rich [2]. This contrasts sharply with conventional RAG systems that often rely on vector databases, which can limit the depth of understanding and reasoning capabilities.

#### Performance and Adaptability

One of the standout features of GraphRAG is its demonstrated improvement in question-and-answer performance, particularly for complex queries. Studies have shown that it outperforms baseline RAG systems, making it a valuable tool for applications requiring advanced reasoning [1]. Moreover, the technology is designed for rapid adaptation to new domains, which enhances its versatility in various fields, including scientific research and data discovery [4].

GraphRAG is accessible through Microsoft Discovery, a platform built on Azure that provides users with tools for evaluating RAG-based systems, such as BenchmarkQED. This accessibility allows researchers and developers to leverage the capabilities of GraphRAG without extensive setup or infrastructure [4].

#### Addressing Challenges with Knowledge Graphs

The integration of knowledge graphs in GraphRAG effectively addresses several unique challenges posed by graph-structured data. These include dealing with diverse formats and domain-specific relational knowledge, which are often obstacles in traditional data retrieval systems [2]. The approach to query-focused summarization, which involves constructing a graph index using a language model to derive an entity knowledge graph from source documents, further enhances the system's ability to generate precise and relevant responses [5].

#### Areas for Further Exploration

Despite its advantages, there are still open questions regarding GraphRAG's comparative performance metrics against other RAG systems. A detailed analysis of its effectiveness across various tasks and domains is necessary to fully understand its strengths and limitations. Additionally, while GraphRAG shows promise, insights into its scalability in real-world applications, especially when handling large datasets or diverse knowledge domains, remain limited. Understanding potential implementation challenges is also crucial for users considering adopting this technology.

In conclusion, GraphRAG represents a significant advancement in the field of Retrieval Augmented Generation by leveraging knowledge graphs to enhance language model reasoning capabilities. Its structured approach, improved performance, and adaptability make it a compelling choice for complex information retrieval tasks.
